description.narrative: The project implores to consolidate and deepen the previous project achieved outcomes on marginalized women as right holders. This project therefore will be hinged on three intervention areas: 1. Transformative skills trainings in Gender equity and Diversity (GED), leadership and civic values, life skills.eg resilience and positive coping, peace <(>&<)> conflict management, advocacy processes. PACHEDO will facilitate 18 women’s rights advocacy groups (WRAGs) of 25- 30 members. The trainings will build self-esteem, developskills and attitudes to appreciate gender equality and engage men and other stakeholders to realize zero tolerance to male dominance, violence against women access to productive resources, health and education services. The civic values willempower right holders to competently interface with policy makers, enforcers at the sub-county to open space for women rights fulfilment and participationin governance. 2. The women’s rights awareness and activism (local, community and institutional activism through role model men methodology). The 18 women Rights Advocacy pressure groups (WRAGs) will be trained on women basic human rights and legal instruments asprovided in CEDAW, constitution of Uganda, land policies and resolutions that protect women’s rights especially the social economicrights, access to productive resources. The various government systems are mandated as duty bearers and community support structures such as cultural, religious leaders as safety nets in protecting and respondingto women right protracted abuses, exploitation and violence. Efforts to intensify on community engagements and action based advocacy for social change and inclusion through civic education and public awareness campaigns will be facilitated on women set rights agendas, identified policy gaps, abuse and violations that will influence policies and decisions to improve enforcement of the legal instruments. The role model men will reach out to fellow men to challenge the violent actions of men and promote Gender equity and Diversity for peaceful co-existence. 3. The social economic empowerment. PACHEDO will train 18 self-help groups on VSLA methodology, business and entrepreneurship skills encourage women to save, borrow to self finance their innovative micro enterprises. Specialized trainings, mentorship in selected market led micro enterprises such as soap making, bakery, piggery including VSLA Kits that will be provided. These will strengthen marginalized women economically, provide employment, increase their personal and household incomes, boost negotiation power, promote social and family cohesion, recognition, inclusion for peaceful co-existence. The overall objective will be to strengthen resilience of marginalized women (rights holders 19-60yrs) in promoting Gender equality and inclusion for improved access to productive resources, social services and civic participation in Bungatira Sub County. By the end of the project, the following changes will be expected to be achieved: At least 85% of marginalized women are aware of their rights and actively participate in voicing and demanding for fulfillment of deprived rights to access productive resources and social services as provided in CEDAW, Uganda constitution, and in government service delivery guidelines such as health, education. Women should not only participate, but proactively engage in civic education and public awareness that impact-fully change attitudes of men, families and communities to zero tolerance to negative and discriminatory cultural, religious practices for improved social relationships, that permit women to gain political space and engage in inclusiveleadership and development programmes. At least 80% of the marginalized women in the 18 self help groups are engaged in social economic activities for dignified employment and demonstrate increased earnings and incomes at individual and household level that should stabilize social relationships and improve their social economic status, promote bargaining power to voice their needs and human rights demands.

participating-org.narrative:
Partners for Community Health and Development Organisation(PACHEDO) is a Not for profit community Based Organization(CBO) that was started in 2007 by a team of volunteer community development workers that included social workers, agriculturalists, healthworkers, teachers, lawyers and Academicians. The organisation was established with aim of supporting communities live a dignified, healthy, and productive life, socio-economically empowered to innovatively meet and demand for their basic needs and rights,which served as the ultimate goal of the organization. Especially targeting the vulnerable population of Gulu comprised of: children, women and Youth exposed to violence and exclusion; Persons living with HIV <(>&<)> AIDS, Adolescents with reproductive healthchallenges, the mentally ill, youth, the older persons and persons with disability in conflict, post conflict and natural disaster affected communities. Since then PACHEDO has been committed in providing services in areas of protection particularly covering transitional justice, GBV prevention and response, child protection, education. Community health targeting Reproductive health and HIV <(>&<)> AIDS care and support, mental health and PSS, WASH and waste management and Nutrition and in Agriculture and sustainable livelihoods of Gulu.
Overtime, PACHEDO has greatly made greater strides in areas of programme development, areas of coverage/operation, human resource development and expansion, finance and systems strengthening. In programmes, there has beenenormous improvement in the quality of generated projects and interventions modes and approaches of delivery such as the community support systems model in promoting all protection activities, other community participatory approaches such CMDRR (Community Managed Disaster Risk Reduction), SMART Agriculture etc. PACHEDO has also managed to recruit qualified personnel in all its programme areas with the lowest staff holding a diploma. In the areas of systems, PACHEDO has also put in place the HR Policy,Financial Policy, child protection, Gender policy among others. PACHEDO has got a qualified Board with a clear and standardised policy manual guideline and Directors signed contracts and playing their roles expected of them. Gender mainstreaming has taken centre stage in the organisation through 50, 50% policy in the recruitment.Women have taken leadership positions and given special considerations at the workplace. PACHEDO is also shifting from spread sheets to QuickBooks before the end of March and bylegality of registration shifting from CBO to NGO by the end of April. 2. ACHIEVEMENTS What have been the principal results in the past three years that contribute to significant, structural, sustained and positive improvement in the lives of men, women, girls and boys suffering from poverty, injustice, insecurity and exclusion?
In the past three years(2015-2017) PACHEDO was able to build up partnerships with donor and technical partners that provided PACHEDO with financial and technical support to appropriately respond to the recovery challenges and human rights issues faced by the vulnerable people during and after the LRA conflict particularly the women, youth, children of all genders (Male and Female) in Gulu especially those womenand girls subjected to various forms of violence and abuse relating to access to their fundamental rights and entitlements such asland, basic services etc and associated vulnerabilities. For instance # 2014-2016 PACHEDO entered into a partnership with VSO (Voluntary Services Overseas) with support from UKAID to provide life skills and psychosocial support to the vulnerable youth-informal students under Youth Development Programme. In this project PACHEDO was able to empower a total of 3,655 LRA conflict affected youthenrolled at all VSO Supported Vocational Institutions with basic conflict mediation and problem solving knowledge and skills includingpeace education and civic values. This enabled the Young People to peacefully adjust and adopt peaceful means of conflictmanagementand promote peaceful co-existence within them, their families, and the entire communities. # 2015-2016, PACHEDO entered in a partnership with Save the Children with support from USAID to scale up GREAT (Gender Roles, Equality and Transformation) innovations. A technical approach and tools that focused at building the capacity adolescent youth-girls and boys, women and community support structures such as the cultural institutions to be able to prevent issues of violence towards women and abuse of their rights. In this case the approach aimed at improving Sexual and reproductive health reducing gender based violence and promoting gender equality in Northern Uganda and strategically focused at working with and ensuring that Boys and Girlsaged 10-19 form equitable gender norms and adopt attitudes and behaviours which positively influence healthy outcomes and reduced gender-based violence. Save the Children/Straight talk foundation based in Gulu provided technical support to PACHEDO andafull package of training on CAC, toolkit, inward looking before outward the knowledge and skills that enabled PACHEDO to equip over 12,000 vulnerable children and women and other community members to defend the Sexual Reproductive Rights of such vulnerable persons in Gulu schools, Households and communities. # 2015-2018, PACHEDO signed a contract with Private Sector Foundation with the funding from EU and later World Bank under ALREP and Skills Development Facility 2 was able to empower over 2300 war affected women and youth-small holder farmers (Male and Female) with livelihood skills particularly crop production, agro processing in different areas, entrepreneurial skills for self reliance, poverty reduction and employment creation. # 2016-2018, PACHEDO joined NGO forum policy advocacy platform in Gulu where 8 PACHEDO staff were trained policy dialogue processes by National NGO forum. The partnership that has build PACHEDO#s capacity of programming, community engagements and right based work and advocacy with the vulnerable people like women and their related protection structures.
